$comment: Triaged performance ceiling for #717, re-measured on 2026-08-20 under CLI 11.3.0 (#744). Lower it when the count drops; never raise it to make CI pass. Enforced by scripts/perf-ratchet.mjs, wired blocking in .github/workflows/harness-quality.yml.
$why: `harness check-perf` was referenced by NO workflow in .github/workflows/ — the audit at 422316b found it among seven such commands. A check that runs nowhere protects nothing, and its passing output is not evidence of anything. This wires it the way #544 wired the entropy scan: an absolute ceiling that may fall and never rise.
$measurement: 237 violations measured at 8c865b5 in a fresh `git worktree`, not in the shared working directory — the entropy count reads 64 high in the main working dir (#700), and a mid-conflict tree returns confident garbage. Command: `harness check-perf` with NO narrowing flag, CLI 11.1.1. Breakdown: 87 cyclomatic-complexity, 58 function-length, 42 file-length, 26 coupling-ratio, 22 nesting-depth, 2 import-count. This composes with ADR 0012 §2, which measured 238 after declaring BOTH `entropy.entryPoints` and `performance.entryPoints`; the standalone command reads `performance.… ?? entropy.…`, so the 67-file denominator is real and the count is not an abstention wearing a number.
$narrowing-flags-are-unusable: Do NOT scope this gate with `--coupling`, `--size`, or `--severity`. Measured on the same tree in the same minute at 8c865b5: a bare `check-perf` reports `x Validation failed (237 issues)`, while `--coupling` and `--size` each report `v validation passed` and exit 0 — over the 28 coupling-ratio and import-count findings that are their own subject. The narrowing flags do not narrow the check, they silence it into a green tick. Scoping the gate to `--coupling` is the tempting move (28 findings is a tractable backlog and 237 is not) and it would have been green forever, over nothing. Filed upstream against harness-engineering. Two guards keep it out: perf-ratchet.mjs treats an implausible collapse as an ABSTENTION (exit 3), and ts/test/workflow-false-green.test.ts asserts the wired invocation carries no narrowing flag.
$delta: 2026-09-09, #812: `maxViolations` is no longer the only rule. On pull requests, `harness-quality.yml` also runs `check-perf` against the merge base in a `$RUNNER_TEMP` worktree and hands both counts to `scripts/perf-ratchet.mjs --base-report`, which fails when the branch introduced violations its base did not have. That is the #703 rule the entropy ratchet already had, ported here because the headroom `$remeasure5` records reached zero — an absolute-only gate at zero headroom fails the next PR that adds one violation whatever that PR's own diff did, and blames whichever branch merges second. The ceiling stays as the BACKSTOP and every rule about it stands: it may fall and never rise, and a PR with a clean delta still fails the build if the total is over it. A base scan with no parseable header, or one that collapsed implausibly, ABSTAINS (exit 3) rather than degrading to the absolute rule; a base that could not be measured is not a base of zero. Verified end to end before merge: 233 head against 233 base passed at +0, and a planted +1 fired with the branch's own delta named.
$headroom: maxViolations is 245 against a measured 237 — 8 violations of deliberate headroom, the same shape the entropy ceiling carries. The headroom exists because the ratchet is an ABSOLUTE total, so concurrent branches consume a shared non-renewable budget that none of them can see (#703, #700). A ceiling pinned exactly to the measured count means the next single green PR that adds one violation fails, which is how a blocking gate becomes wallpaper. Lower it when the count drops; never raise it to make CI pass.
$remeasure: 2026-08-20, #744: 225 violations at c8f412a in a fresh worktree under CLI 11.3.0, against a file that still recorded 237 at 11.1.1. The drop is NOT attributable to 11.3.0 — 11.2.0 reports 225 on the same tree in the same minute, so the move happened at the 11.1.1 -> 11.2.0 boundary and sat unrecorded here for a week. This was the quiet half of the #744 investigation: the gap was 20 against a 245 ceiling, small enough that nobody would have gone looking, where the entropy gap was 120. Both were the same defect — an absolute count whose instrument floats. Ceiling lowered 245 -> 233, preserving this file's own +8 convention (237 -> 245). CONFIRMED by CI on PR #746: the `validate` job resolved the floating pin to 11.3.0 and reported 225 — an exact match with the fresh-worktree measurement, which is the evidence that the worktree method (#700) reproduces CI. A first CI run reported 226; that +1 was this PR's own diff (an inlined instrument check pushed `main` in entropy-ratchet.mjs past the function-length and complexity thresholds) and was removed by extracting `requireMatchingInstrument`, matching the shape perf-ratchet.mjs already used.
$instrument: `harnessCli` is the EXACT version that produced `measuredCount`. The workflows pin `@harness-engineering/cli@11`, a floating major, so the analyzer under this absolute count can change with no commit here. As of #744 that is no longer silent: the `Resolve harness CLI version` step in `harness-quality.yml` resolves the pin and passes `--cli-version` to `scripts/perf-ratchet.mjs`, which ABSTAINS (exit 3) on any disagreement rather than comparing a count to a ceiling calibrated against a different instrument. When the pin resolves to a new version, re-measure in a clean worktree and update this file in the same PR. Do not silence the abstention by deleting `harnessCli`.
$remeasure2: 2026-08-30, the @11 -> @12 pin bump: 227 violations at 3659ea9 in a fresh worktree, and this number is CLI-INDEPENDENT — 11.3.0 and 12.1.0 produce byte-identical `check-perf` output on the same tree in the same minute (47,514 bytes, same md5). So unlike the entropy count, which moved 147 -> 135 across the same bump, nothing here is attributable to the analyzer. The 225 -> 227 delta is ordinary code growth in the eight PRs between c8f412a and 3659ea9. `maxViolations` is deliberately LEFT at 233: the effective headroom tightens 8 -> 6, and raising a ceiling to restore headroom is this file's one forbidden move. `harnessCli` is bumped to 12.1.0 anyway, because `requireMatchingInstrument` compares identity and not the number — leaving it at 11.3.0 would abstain the perf gate (exit 3) on every run once CI resolves @12, turning a passing gate into a permanent no-op. An unmoved count still needs a current instrument stamp.
$remeasure4: 2026-09-08, CLI 12.2.0 -> 12.4.0, and the count DID move — 227 -> 232 — but not because of the analyzer. `check-perf` has now been CLI-independent across four consecutive releases, so the +5 is this repo: five merges landed since 2026-09-01 (#802, #803, #804, #805, #806, #807, #808), each green under the 233 ceiling on its own. Measured on `origin/main` at 3de050d in a detached worktree under a pinned `@harness-engineering/cli@12.4.0`, and confirmed at 232 on PR #811's docs-only branch — identical, as a docs change must be. `maxViolations` is UNCHANGED at 233: raising it is the forbidden move, and the count is under it. THE NUMBER TO READ HERE IS THE HEADROOM: 1. Not 6, not 8 — one violation. The next PR that adds a single function-length or complexity violation fails this gate whatever its own delta, and that is the #703 pathology on the perf side, where the merge-base delta rule does NOT exist yet (#703 landed on the entropy ratchet only). Filed as a follow-up rather than fixed here, because a docs PR is the wrong place to change a blocking gate's semantics. The honest remedy is paydown, not a higher ceiling.
$remeasure3: 2026-09-01, CLI 12.1.0 -> 12.2.0: 227 violations at 6a37557 in the same clean worktree, and this count remains CLI-INDEPENDENT — 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 produce BYTE-IDENTICAL `check-perf` output on the same tree in the same minute (47,514 bytes, matching md5), exactly as 11.3.0 and 12.1.0 did in `$remeasure2`. Nothing here is attributable to the analyzer across three consecutive releases now. `maxViolations` stays at 233 and the effective headroom stays at 6. `harnessCli` is bumped anyway, for the reason `$remeasure2` already spells out: identity, not the number, is what `requireMatchingInstrument` compares, so a stale stamp abstains a gate that is otherwise passing.
$remeasure5: 2026-09-09, CLI 12.4.0 -> 12.6.0 (found by the abstention turning `validate` red on PR #824): `check-perf` is CLI-INDEPENDENT for a FIFTH consecutive release — 12.4.0 and 12.6.0 produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output on the same tree in the same minute (48,800 bytes, same md5). The count moved 232 -> 233, and per the five-release record that is this repo, not the analyzer: ten merges landed between 3de050d and e63a533 (#811, #813-#822), each green under 233 on its own. Measured at 456a8ac (= `origin/main` e63a533 plus a mise.toml change that no scanner reads) in a detached worktree. `maxViolations` is UNCHANGED at 233. THE HEADROOM IS NOW ZERO. `$remeasure4` said the number to read was headroom 1 and that the next PR adding a single violation would fail this gate whatever its own delta; that PR has landed, the gate passed it at 233 == 233, and the next one will not. This is #812 exactly, and it is now not a forecast. The honest remedies remain paydown (lower the count) or the merge-base delta rule #703 gave the entropy ratchet — never a higher ceiling. Recorded here because the abstention forced a same-PR re-stamp; the semantics change belongs in #812.
$remeasure6: 2026-09-09, CLI 12.6.0 -> 12.7.0: 233 violations at 242468b in a detached worktree outside the checkout, under an explicitly pinned `@harness-engineering/cli@12.7.0`. `harness check-perf` reports `Validation failed (233 issues)` — the same count the 12.6.0 stamp carried, so this count stays CLI-INDEPENDENT across a SIXTH consecutive release. `maxViolations` stays at 233 and the effective headroom stays at ZERO; #812's merge-base delta rule is what makes that survivable, and paydown rather than a higher ceiling is still the only legitimate way to restore headroom. `harnessCli` is bumped anyway, for the reason $remeasure2 spells out: identity, not the number, is what `requireMatchingInstrument` compares, so a stale stamp abstains a gate that is otherwise passing.
